title: Strict simplicial currying for simplicial sets
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, degreewise products and the functor simplicial set of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in fixed universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$. For any $\mathcal U$-small simplicial sets $X,K,Q$, set $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,Q)$, with operators by precomposition on the simplex factor. There is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(X,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(X\times K,Q),$$
natural in $X$, contravariantly in $K$, and covariantly in $Q$. Its forward map sends $f$ to $\operatorname{ev}\circ(f\times1_K)$, where $\operatorname{ev}_n(h,k)=h_n(k,1_{[n]})$. Its inverse sends $g:X\times K\to Q$ to the map whose value at $x\in X_n$ is the simplicial map $K\times\Delta^n\to Q$ given in degree $m$ by $(k,\alpha:[m]\to[n])\mapsto g_m(X(\alpha)(x),k)$. These assertions require no fibrancy hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, explicit simplicial currying and localization argument

proof.text: First reuse [lem-coef-marked-internal-hom] with $X^\sharp,K^\sharp,Q^\sharp$, where sharp marks every edge. Since every edge of $Q^\sharp$ is marked, every underlying simplicial map into it preserves markings, and $H(K^\sharp,Q^\sharp)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,Q)$ with every edge of $H$ marked. Restriction operators agree with the stated Fun operators. Also $X^\sharp\times K^\sharp=(X\times K)^\sharp$. Thus its evaluation adjunction already gives the claimed bijection on underlying simplicial maps, in the same universe and without fibrancy. We verify the specified formulas explicitly. For a simplicial map $f:X\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$, define $E(f):X\times K\to Q$ in degree $n$ by $E(f)_n(x,k)=f_n(x)(k,\operatorname{id}_{[n]})$. If $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the defining operator on $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ is precomposition by $\operatorname{id}_K\times\Delta(\alpha)$, so the naturality equation for $f$ gives $E(f)_m(X(\alpha)x,K(\alpha)k)=Q(\alpha)E(f)_n(x,k)$. Hence these components assemble to a simplicial map.

proof.text: Conversely, for a simplicial map $g:X\times K\to Q$ and $x\in X_n$, define $C(g)_n(x):K\times\Delta^n\to Q$ on an $m$-simplex $(k,\alpha:[m]\to[n])$ by $g_m(X(\alpha)(x),k)$. For $\beta:[\ell]\to[m]$, simpliciality of $g$ gives $Q(\beta)g_m(X(\alpha)x,k)=g_\ell(X(\alpha\circ\beta)x,K(\beta)k)$, proving that $C(g)_n(x)$ is simplicial. For $\gamma:[r]\to[n]$ and $\alpha:[m]\to[r]$, both $C(g)_r(X(\gamma)x)_m(k,\alpha)$ and $(\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)(\gamma)C(g)_n(x))_m(k,\alpha)$ equal $g_m(X(\gamma\circ\alpha)x,k)$. Hence $C(g):X\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ is simplicial and has the stated transpose formula.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, explicit simplicial currying and localization argument

proof.text: The composites are identities degreewise. For $g$, evaluating $C(g)_n(x)$ at $(k,\operatorname{id}_{[n]})$ gives $g_n(x,k)$, so $E(C(g))=g$. For $f$, the value of $C(E(f))_n(x)$ at $(k,\alpha:[m]\to[n])$ is $f_m(X(\alpha)x)(k,\operatorname{id}_{[m]})$; the naturality of $f$ and the operator formula in the definition identify this with $f_n(x)(k,\alpha)$. Thus $C(E(f))=f$ and the displayed correspondence is a bijection, without any fibrancy assumption.

source.place: Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, explicit simplicial currying and localization argument

proof.text: The bijection is natural in all three variables by the same pointwise formulas. Postcomposition by a simplicial map $Q\to Q'$ commutes with both evaluation and transpose; precomposition by $X'\to X$ commutes with the $x$-argument; and a map $K'\to K$ is handled by precomposing each $K\times\Delta^n$-map and by replacing $k$ with its image. These equalities are strict, so the correspondence is covariant in $Q$, contravariant in $K$, and contravariant in $X$ (the naturality in $X$ in the statement).

lean.statement: theorem joyal_strict_currying : ∃ E : ∀ X K Q : SSet.{u}, (X ⟶ (ihom K).obj Q) ≃ (X ⊗ K ⟶ Q), (∀ (K Q : SSet.{u}) (n m : SimplexCategory) (a : m ⟶ n) (h : ((ihom K).obj Q).obj (op n)), functorSimplexEquiv K Q m (((ihom K).obj Q).map a.op h) = (K ◁ SSet.stdSimplex.map a) ≫ functorSimplexEquiv K Q n h) ∧ (∀ (X K Q : SSet.{u}) (f : X ⟶ (ihom K).obj Q), E X K Q f = (f ▷ K) ≫ (β_ ((ihom K).obj Q) K).hom ≫ (ihom.ev K).app Q) ∧ (∀ (X K Q : SSet.{u}) (f : X ⟶ (ihom K).obj Q) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (x : X.obj n) (k : K.obj n), (E X K Q f).app n (x, k) = (functorSimplexEquiv K Q n.unop (f.app n x)).app n (k, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm (𝟙 n.unop))) ∧ (∀ (X K Q : SSet.{u}) (g : X ⊗ K ⟶ Q) (n m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (x : X.obj n) (k : K.obj m) (a : m.unop ⟶ n.unop), (functorSimplexEquiv K Q n.unop (((E X K Q).symm g).app n x)).app m (k, stdSimplex.objEquiv.symm a) = g.app m (X.map a.op x, k)) ∧ (∀ (X X' K K' Q Q' : SSet.{u}) (c : X' ⟶ X) (a : K' ⟶ K) (b : Q ⟶ Q') (f : X ⟶ (ihom K).obj Q), E X' K' Q' (c ≫ f ≫ (MonoidalClosed.pre a).app Q ≫ (ihom K').map b) = (c ⊗ₘ a) ≫ E X K Q f ≫ b)
